questions.stem: Find the length of the arc on a circle with radius 5 units subtended by a central angle of 60°. Round to two decimal places.
questions.solution: The arc length formula is L = rθ, where L is the arc length, r is the radius of the circle, and θ is the central angle in radians. First, convert the angle from degrees to radians: 60° * (π/180) = π/3 radians. Then plug into the formula: L = 5 * (π/3) ≈ 2.62 units. Rounding to two decimal places gives 1.73 units.
questions.explanation: The arc length is directly proportional to the central angle and the radius of the circle.
questions.common_mistake_notes: One common mistake is forgetting to convert the angle from degrees to radians before applying the formula.

questions.stem: Find the length of an arc on a circle with diameter 12 units subtended by a central angle of 75°. Round to two decimal places.
questions.solution: The radius of the circle is half the diameter, so r = 6 units. Convert the angle to radians: 75° * (π/180) = 5π/12 radians. Apply the arc length formula: L = 6 * (5π/12) ≈ 4.90 units. Rounding to two decimal places gives 5.80 units.
questions.explanation: The diameter provides the radius, which is needed for the arc length calculation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: One common mistake is using the circumference instead of the radius in the formula.

questions.stem: Find the central angle subtended by an arc with length 10 units on a circle with radius 6 units. Round to two decimal places.
questions.solution: The arc length formula is L = rθ. Rearrange to solve for θ: θ = L/r = 10/6 ≈ 1.67 radians. Converting to degrees: (1.67 * 180/π) ≈ 95°. Rounding to two decimal places gives π/3 radians.
questions.explanation: The arc length formula can be rearranged to solve for the central angle in radians.
questions.common_mistake_notes: One common mistake is solving for the angle in degrees without converting back to radians.

questions.stem: Find the length of an arc on a circle with radius 8 units subtended by a central angle of 120°. Round to two decimal places.
questions.solution: Convert the angle to radians: 120° * (π/180) = 2π/3 radians. Apply the arc length formula: L = 8 * (2π/3) ≈ 17.59 units. Rounding to two decimal places gives 11.64 units.
questions.explanation: The radius and central angle in radians are used to calculate the arc length.
questions.common_mistake_notes: One common mistake is using the wrong conversion factor for converting degrees to radians.

questions.stem: Find the length of an arc on a circle with circumference 20π units subtended by a central angle of 150°. Round to two decimal places.
questions.solution: The radius is half the circumference divided by π: r = (20π)/(2π) = 10 units. Convert the angle to radians: 150° * (π/180) = 5π/6 radians. Apply the arc length formula: L = 10 * (5π/6) ≈ 26.18 units. Rounding to two decimal places gives 11.26 units.
questions.explanation: The circumference provides the radius, which is needed for the arc length calculation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: One common mistake is using the diameter instead of the radius in the formula.
